title: Overlooking the One Thing That Changes Everything
speaker: Aaron Brockett
goal: By the end, men commit to identifying and surrendering their 'one thing' to Christ.
scripture_instructions: Ask one person to read Mark 10:13-22 and another to read verses 23-31. Pause briefly after each to let it settle.

icebreakers.label: A
icebreakers.question: Share the most extravagant or unusual gift you've ever received.
icebreakers.note: Light-hearted way to introduce giving and receiving.

icebreakers.label: B
icebreakers.question: When have you had to give up something big to gain something important?

icebreakers.label: C
icebreakers.question: What's one possession you can't imagine giving up?
icebreakers.note: Pushes men to honesty about attachment.

sections.title: The Rich Young Ruler
sections.setup: The rich young ruler approached Jesus, seeking eternal life, but had a glaring attachment. He was successful yet couldn't part with his wealth, revealing the one thing he held above all. Jesus loved him enough to tell him what he didn't want to hear.
sections.say: Let's start by looking at the rich young ruler, a man who ran to Jesus but couldn't commit fully.

questions.ask: What drove you to your last encounter with God asking for assurance?
questions.lead: The ruler ran to Jesus seeking assurance of eternal life.
questions.probe: Is there a recurring insecurity driving your requests?

questions.ask: What is your 'one thing' you fear would break you if lost?
questions.lead: Despite his wealth, the ruler lacked something crucial.
questions.probe: When did you first realize this could be your 'one thing'?

questions.ask: Who last told hard truth to you because they love you?
questions.lead: Jesus loved the ruler enough to tell him hard truths.
questions.probe: How did you initially react, and what have you done since?

questions.ask: When have you mistaken action for assurance in your spiritual life?
questions.lead: The ruler wanted an achievement-based answer from Jesus.
questions.probe: How did you recognize the difference?

reflection_questions: What drove me to my last encounter with God seeking assurance?
What is my 'one thing' I fear losing?
Who last told me hard truth out of love?
When have I mistaken action for assurance in my faith journey?

sections.title: Jesus' Challenge and Love
sections.setup: Jesus noted that the kingdom is a gift to be received, not achieved. Yet, he laid a direct challenge before the ruler that was too costly in the young man's eyes. His possessions held him more than he held them.
sections.say: Jesus presented both challenge and love to the ruler, showing genuine concern for his soul above all else.

questions.ask: What aspect of your faith do you still approach as if you need to achieve something?
questions.lead: The kingdom of God is to be received, like a child.
questions.probe: How does this affect your view of God's grace?

questions.ask: Has God ever asked you to take a step that seemed too big at the time?
questions.lead: Jesus proposed a radical step to the ruler.
questions.probe: How did you rationalize any resistance?

questions.ask: When have you walked away from a challenge with God, and did you revisit the decision?
questions.lead: The young ruler left saddened by Jesus' request.
questions.probe: What emotion surrounded your decision at that time?

questions.ask: Who in your life do you find difficult to lovingly challenge, and why?
questions.lead: Jesus extends love even while challenging the ruler.
questions.probe: What would make it easier to have that conversation?

reflection_questions: What aspect of my faith do I still try to achieve?
Has God ever asked me for a seemingly impossible step?
When have I walked away from a God challenge?
Who do I find difficult to lovingly challenge, and why?

sections.title: The Call to Surrender
sections.setup: Jesus invites us to let go of what we've made ultimate, surrender, and trust him as our true provider. Our attachments can blind us to God's greater purpose, but surrender leads to true freedom.
sections.say: Surrendering fully to God means letting go of our functional saviors, those false securities we cling to.

questions.ask: What's one area you hesitate to let Christ rule?
questions.lead: To follow Christ is to surrender completely.
questions.probe: What's at stake for you in this area?

questions.ask: How do you practice generosity in a way that stretches you?
questions.lead: Faithful, consistent generosity can break idolatry.
questions.probe: Does your current approach truly challenge your comfort?

questions.ask: What possession or status do you sense God challenging you to hold loosely now?
questions.lead: Attachment to possessions can rightly orient our hearts.
questions.probe: What would holding it loosely change in your life?

questions.ask: What securities in your life do you prioritize over your relationship with God?
questions.lead: Jesus challenges us to question our securities.
questions.probe: What patterns emerge when these are threatened?

reflection_questions: What area do I hesitate to let Christ rule?
How do I practice generosity that stretches me?
What possession or status do I feel challenged to hold loosely?
What securities do I prioritize over my relationship with God?

closing_go_around: Let's each share one thing we're choosing to hold more loosely this week.
prayer: Ask God to reveal and help you release the 'one thing' that you tend to hold too tightly.

cheat_sheet.dynamic: Someone is quiet about a personal 'one thing'.
cheat_sheet.response: Ask if there's anything they feel called to share, no pressure, just openness.

cheat_sheet.dynamic: Discussion sways to financial status as defining success.
cheat_sheet.response: Recenter around what Jesus defines as true riches: relationship with Him.

cheat_sheet.dynamic: Someone justifies holding onto a possession tightly.
cheat_sheet.response: Gently ask what peace those possessions actually bring compared to God.

cheat_sheet.dynamic: A participant minimizes their role in God's kingdom.
cheat_sheet.response: Affirm their unique place in the church community, noting their gifts.

cheat_sheet.dynamic: A man doubts any significant change from surrender.
cheat_sheet.response: Share a story of transformation through surrender and God's faithfulness.

key_themes: Faith as a gift, not an accomplishment.
True wealth is counted in God's kingdom.
Generosity breaks the hold of idolatry.
commitment_prompt: This week, identify your 'one thing' and choose to open your grips on it, sharing with a trusted friend.
thesis: Overlooking the one thing that could change everything is costly.
sensitivities: Discussing wealth may touch on personal financial struggles.
obstacle: What makes you guard your 'one thing' even from God's touch this week?
carry: Next week, ask each other about the 'one thing' you committed to let go.
